bugs.what: After refusing the Ironbound and having Prior Halm have them walked off Stilt Row (Church rep +1, Brother Osk approved, narratively framed as the compassionate/right call), the journal marked 'Quest failed: The Mission's Order.' The 'failed' tag contradicts the positive in-fiction outcome and could make a player think they did something wrong when they didn't.
bugs.where: The Priory of the Gray Church / tell Halm what the Ironbound mean to do

bugs.what: status always shows an 'Old Court Verses: 0/3 (unexplored: the ring-ditch, the king's causeway, the mere-stone)' tracker alongside the real 'Verses' tracker, but across ~290 turns of thorough play (talking to every NPC found, reading every board/ledger, visiting Last Light, Fenmarch/Reedholm in full, and all of Ashwood) no dialogue, quest, or notice ever mentioned it. It reads as a second, unexplained quest line cluttering the status screen.

Whether a hostile encounter can be avoided/talked down is inconsistent and unsignaled: the gray husk at the cairn explicitly said 'It does not stir unless struck,' but the ash wolf at Twin Stones gave no such cue and offered only an attack option — after killing it the game revealed 'Lys disapproves,' with no way to have known in advance that this fight (unlike others) had a companion-approval cost or perhaps an alternate resolution.

The King's Strongroom puzzle (opening the strongbox) offers only might ('force it') or grace ('pick it') checks, with no will/persuasion option, even though the steward's shade guarding it literally monologues about words vs. iron ('a man's word once needed iron behind it to be believed') and virtually every other obstacle in the game up to this point had offered a will-based path for a talker build.

confusions: No signal anywhere (intro, status, or notices) of how much of the 300-turn budget one hold costs. Playing exactly as instructed (talk to everyone, follow up, explore fully, travel beyond the first place) consumed ~290 of 300 turns finishing just the Vale of Ash (plus a side trip to neighboring Fenmarch) — one hold out of nine, and the game's own log states 'six holds, six unrested griefs. Rest three... any opens Coldpass' is only a mid-game gate, not the ending. A thorough, non-wasteful playthrough cannot reach *** WIN/*** LOSE in 300 turns; there is no way to have known that going in.
The 'Old Court Verses' tracker (see bugs) never surfaced as reachable content, so it reads as a confusing dead status line rather than a discoverable quest.

It was never clear whether sealing vs. leaving the barrow doors open (the final choice at the throne) has any mechanical stakes beyond flavor text and a +1 Gray Church reputation tick — the reeve, priest, and king all frame it as consequential ('what walks free' vs. 'grief undone'), but no downstream effect was shown before or after the choice.
suggestions: Give players an explicit pacing cue (e.g. in the seed-19 intro or the status header) for how many turns a hold typically takes, so exploration depth can be budgeted against the 300-turn ending goal.
Change 'Quest failed: The Mission's Order' to a neutral/positive completion tag when the resolution the player chose is the one companions approve of and factions reward.
Either give 'Old Court Verses' a discoverable thread in Act I or hide it from status until the player has some lead on it.
Signal consistently (or consistently omit) whether a fight can be avoided/talked past before the player commits, especially where a companion will later register disapproval.

Add a will-based option to the strongbox in the King's Strongroom (or any similarly 'iron only' puzzle) so a dedicated talker/Envoy build always has a dialogue-flavored route, matching the rest of the game's design.

The crown+verses combined ending at the throne (score +35, unanimous companion approval) is excellent payoff for thorough, curious, promise-keeping play — more moments this well-telegraphed and rewarding would make the loop worth its length.
